title: # Crowd-only follow-through — round 4, 23 October 2026
inventory_note: Fourth cohort covers20 of remaining65;80 reviewed overall,45 remain. Newly eligible fuck-me-sideways included here.

checks.notes: Surprise exclamation; foreign witness.
Campaign pairs fruit-and-veg title with fruit-and-vegetables body.
Protesters use grub as a hostile personal label.
Magistrate pairs show-pony with exhibitionist in streaking case.
Small coins in a payment discussion are called shrapnel.
Speaker contrasts evidence-based family history with spinning-a-yarn.
Researcher explains weather abbreviation and its cold full expression.
Queensland correspondent supplies the exact weather expression; researcher explains its very-cold meaning.
Cricketer's week is described as full-on and intense.
Witness recounts being called piss-weak and gutless for refusing action.
Trainer is called laid-back and relaxed by nature.
Tourism guide explicitly lists Brissie among Brisbane nicknames.

checks.publisher: UNSW Australians at War Film Archive
checks.notes: Captain answers a summons with goodo and complies.
Police refer to guardrail damage by a hoon-driver and hoon-driving.
Article pairs rollies with roll-your-own cigarettes.
Party source says we're-cooked when discussing electoral defeat and danger.
Speaker directly pairs getting-shitty with angry and agitated.
Court report explicitly explains towel-up as beating people up.
Speaker-teacher explains sentence-final hey as agreement-seeking tag or habitual ending.
Father's bloody-hell response is explicitly framed as surprise.

proposals: Keep exact-frame gaps: bare brass-monkeys predicate versus weather/full expression; compound hoon-driver versus general noun; physical towel-up versus sports sense.
Fuck-me-sideways has foreign publisher surprise evidence only; no new Australian-use certification.
Bloody-hell witness shows positive surprise; dismay is a separate use, not a contradiction.
